source.title: Cyclic and Randomized Stepsizes Invoke Heavier Tails in SGD
source.authors: M. Gürbüzbalaban; Yuanhan Hu; Umut Simsekli; Lingjiong Zhu

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares SGD step-size schedules using training–test loss and accuracy differences and estimates tail indices, bearing on the claim’s broad generalization-gap and measured-property subject. It does not test a specific mapped version.
record.gate_note: Theoretical tail-index comparisons and deep-learning results are the paper’s own. Cited prior work on generalization and step-size schedules is not recorded as a result. Table values are assigned by their visible schedule and η̂ groupings.
record.test_reason: The study tests how SGD step-size schedules affect tail indices and generalization gaps, but none of V1–V8 names that comparison. Tail index does not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness. Batch-size experiments measure tails in linear regression, not V5's held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors establish heavier tails under alternative step-size schedules subject to their theoretical assumptions, and suggest that this may help explain their performance. Their deep-learning experiments show that Markovian schedules perform best in some conditions, while explicitly acknowledging exceptions to the tail-index/generalization association. This is a proposed explanation, not a demonstrated causal mechanism.
record.recipe_differences: Studies step-size schedules and tail-index/generalization associations; the mapped versions concern memorization, width, architecture, optimizer comparisons, batch size, dropout, sharpness, and memorized-example removal.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported generalization differences and tail indices vary with step-size schedule and center η̂; the text notes a non-monotonic exception at η̂=0.06 for MNIST and an accuracy exception at η̂=0.11 for VGG11.

fits_no_version.finding: Step-size schedules change SGD tail-index estimates and loss gaps. On MNIST at η̂=0.08 and 0.09, Markovian p=0.5 has the smallest tail index and loss gap; at η̂=0.06, constant steps have the smallest loss gap despite heavier tails under several alternatives. On CIFAR-10, the smallest tail index does not consistently identify the smallest loss gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD step-size scheduling affects tail heaviness and training–test loss gaps, with an imperfect association that depends on the model and learning-rate setting.

fits_no_version.finding: For linear regression with Gaussian inputs, the theory makes tail index increase with batch size when the index is at least one, and decrease with parameter dimension. Figure 3 reports increasing tail indices for batches 5, 10, and 15; it does not report held-out performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the stated linear-regression assumptions, batch size and parameter dimension affect SGD tail heaviness.

record.problems: The deep-learning evidence covers only a 3-layer fully connected MNIST network and VGG11 on CIFAR10. The paper states that the tail-index/generalization relation is not a perfect straight line and identifies exceptions. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the table results.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 and Table 2 also report training error, test error, training accuracy, test accuracy, and accuracy difference. Those additional metrics were omitted to prioritize the test–train error difference and tail-index within the row limit; their values are in the same tables.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and chance-level held-out accuracy compared with natural-label generalization under the same recipe.
Network-width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks on the same image task, including local-connectivity interventions and initialization comparisons.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, including tuning, weight decay, and optimizer switching.
Held-out performance for different batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout interventions, small-data effects, excessive dropout, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation tolerance and its ranking of generalization gaps against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All 27 numerical pairs and their schedule assignments match the supplied tables. Their states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because they measure none of those versions. The fully connected network and VGG11 use different datasets, so their results cannot establish V3. A smaller training–test gap need not mean better held-out performance: at MNIST η̂=0.09, Markovian p=0.5 has the smallest loss gap, but constant steps achieve higher test accuracy, 97.71% versus 97.52%. Additional table metrics are already declared in rows_left_out; no omitted result tests a mapped version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons and their tuning or weight-decay conditions.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its comparison to norm- or margin-based measures.
